passages.text: For behold, the Lord GOD of Hosts is about to remove from Jerusalem and Judah both supply and support: the whole supply of food and water, the mighty man and the warrior, the judge and the prophet, the soothsayer and the elder, the commander of fifty and the dignitary, the counselor, the cunning magician, and the clever enchanter.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD of Hosts is the ruler of all.
He will act in Jerusalem and Judah.
He will take away every support from them.
He will remove all food and all water.
He will remove the mighty man.
He will remove the warrior.
He will remove the judge.
He will remove the prophet.
He will remove the soothsayer.
He will remove the elder.
He will remove the commander of fifty.
He will remove the dignitary.
He will remove the counselor.
He will remove the skilled craftsman.
He will remove the clever enchanter.
passages.original: כִּי֩ הִנֵּ֨ה הָאָד֜וֹן יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת מֵסִ֤יר מִירוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ וּמִ֣יהוּדָ֔ה מַשְׁעֵ֖ן וּמַשְׁעֵנָ֑ה כֹּ֚ל מִשְׁעַן־ לֶ֔חֶם וְכֹ֖ל מִשְׁעַן־ מָֽיִם׃ גִּבּ֖וֹר וְאִ֣ישׁ מִלְחָמָ֑ה שׁוֹפֵ֥ט וְנָבִ֖יא וְקֹסֵ֥ם וְזָקֵֽן׃ שַׂר־ חֲמִשִּׁ֖ים וּנְשׂ֣וּא פָנִ֑ים וְיוֹעֵ֛ץ וַחֲכַ֥ם חֲרָשִׁ֖ים וּנְב֥וֹן לָֽחַשׁ׃

passages.text: “I will make mere lads their leaders, and children will rule over them.”
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD of Hosts will act.
He will give Jerusalem and Judah new leaders.
These leaders will be mere boys.
Children will rule over the people.
passages.original: וְנָתַתִּ֥י נְעָרִ֖ים שָׂרֵיהֶ֑ם וְתַעֲלוּלִ֖ים יִמְשְׁלוּ־ בָֽם׃

passages.text: The people will oppress one another, man against man, neighbor against neighbor; the young will rise up against the old, and the base against the honorable.
passages.sermon:
The people will oppress each other.
Each man will act against another man.
Each person will act against his neighbor.
Young people will rise up against old people.
Those who are base will rise up against those who are honorable.
passages.original: וְנִגַּ֣שׂ הָעָ֔ם אִ֥ישׁ בְּאִ֖ישׁ וְאִ֣ישׁ בְּרֵעֵ֑הוּ יִרְהֲב֗וּ הַנַּ֙עַר֙ בַּזָּקֵ֔ן וְהַנִּקְלֶ֖ה בַּנִּכְבָּֽד׃

passages.text: A man will seize his brother within his father’s house: “You have a cloak—you be our leader! Take charge of this heap of rubble.”
passages.sermon:
A man will grab his brother.
They will be inside their father’s house.
The man will say to his brother, “You have a cloak.
Be our leader.
Take control of this ruin.”
passages.original: כִּֽי־ יִתְפֹּ֨שׂ אִ֤ישׁ בְּאָחִיו֙ בֵּ֣ית אָבִ֔יו שִׂמְלָ֣ה לְכָ֔ה קָצִ֖ין תִּֽהְיֶה־ לָּ֑נוּ וְהַמַּכְשֵׁלָ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את תַּ֥חַת יָדֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: On that day he will cry aloud: “I am not a healer. I have no food or clothing in my house. Do not make me leader of the people!”
passages.sermon:
A man in Jerusalem will speak on that day.
He will say, “I am not a healer.”
He will say, “I have no food in my house.”
He will say, “I have no clothing in my house.”
He will say, “Do not make me the leader of the people.”
passages.original: יִשָּׂא֩ בַיּ֨וֹם הַה֤וּא׀ לֵאמֹר֙ לֹא־ אֶהְיֶ֣ה חֹבֵ֔שׁ וּבְבֵיתִ֕י אֵ֥ין לֶ֖חֶם וְאֵ֣ין שִׂמְלָ֑ה לֹ֥א תְשִׂימֻ֖נִי קְצִ֥ין עָֽם׃

passages.text: For Jerusalem has stumbled and Judah has fallen because they spoke and acted against the LORD, defying His glorious presence.
passages.sermon:
Jerusalem has stumbled.
Judah has fallen.
They spoke against the LORD.
They acted against the LORD.
They defied His glorious presence.
passages.original: כִּ֤י כָשְׁלָה֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם וִיהוּדָ֖ה נָפָ֑ל כִּֽי־ לְשׁוֹנָ֤ם וּמַֽעַלְלֵיהֶם֙ אֶל־ יְהוָ֔ה לַמְר֖וֹת עֵנֵ֥י כְבוֹדֽוֹ׃

passages.text: The expression on their faces testifies against them, and like Sodom they flaunt their sin; they do not conceal it. Woe to them, for they have brought disaster upon themselves.
passages.sermon:
Their faces show their guilt.
Their expressions reveal their sin.
They act like the people of Sodom.
They openly display their wrongdoing.
They do not try to hide their sin.
Disaster will come to them.
They have brought this trouble on themselves.
passages.original: הַכָּרַ֤ת פְּנֵיהֶם֙ עָ֣נְתָה בָּ֔ם וְחַטָּאתָ֛ם כִּסְדֹ֥ם הִגִּ֖ידוּ לֹ֣א כִחֵ֑דוּ א֣וֹי לְנַפְשָׁ֔ם כִּֽי־ גָמְל֥וּ לָהֶ֖ם רָעָֽה׃

passages.text: Tell the righteous it will be well with them, for they will enjoy the fruit of their labor.
passages.sermon:
The righteous are people who do what is right in God's eyes.
Tell the righteous this message.
It will be well with them.
They will enjoy the fruit of their labor.
God will reward them for their good actions.
passages.original: אִמְר֥וּ צַדִּ֖יק כִּי־ ט֑וֹב כִּֽי־ פְרִ֥י מַעַלְלֵיהֶ֖ם יֹאכֵֽלוּ׃

passages.text: Woe to the wicked; disaster is upon them! For they will be repaid with what their hands have done.
passages.sermon:
The wicked person does evil.
Disaster will come to the wicked person.
The wicked person will receive what he has done.
He will be repaid for his actions.
passages.original: א֖וֹי לְרָשָׁ֣ע רָ֑ע כִּֽי־ גְמ֥וּל יָדָ֖יו יֵעָ֥שֶׂה לּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Youths oppress My people, and women rule over them. O My people, your guides mislead you; they turn you from your paths.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
Young people oppress My people.
Women rule over My people.
My people, your leaders mislead you.
Your guides turn you away from the right path.
passages.original: עַמִּי֙ נֹגְשָׂ֣יו מְעוֹלֵ֔ל וְנָשִׁ֖ים מָ֣שְׁלוּ ב֑וֹ עַמִּי֙ מְאַשְּׁרֶ֣יךָ מַתְעִ֔ים וְדֶ֥רֶךְ אֹֽרְחֹתֶ֖יךָ בִּלֵּֽעוּ׃ס

passages.text: The LORD arises to contend; He stands to judge the people.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is present.
The LORD stands up to argue.
The LORD stands to judge the nations.
The LORD acts as judge over the people.
passages.original: נִצָּ֥ב לָרִ֖יב יְהוָ֑ה וְעֹמֵ֖ד לָדִ֥ין עַמִּֽים׃

passages.text: The LORD brings this charge against the elders and leaders of His people: “You have devoured the vineyard; the plunder of the poor is in your houses.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the judge of all people.
The LORD brings a charge against the elders and leaders of His people.
You elders and leaders have destroyed the vineyard.
You have taken what belongs to the poor.
You keep the plunder of the poor in your houses.
passages.original: יְהוָה֙ בְּמִשְׁפָּ֣ט יָב֔וֹא עִם־ זִקְנֵ֥י עַמּ֖וֹ וְשָׂרָ֑יו וְאַתֶּם֙ בִּֽעַרְתֶּ֣ם הַכֶּ֔רֶם גְּזֵלַ֥ת הֶֽעָנִ֖י בְּבָתֵּיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Why do you crush My people and grind the faces of the poor?” declares the Lord GOD of Hosts.
passages.sermon:
The Lord GOD of Hosts speaks.
He asks a question.
He says, “Why do you crush My people?
Why do you grind the faces of the poor?”
passages.original: מַלָּכֶם תְּדַכְּא֣וּ עַמִּ֔י וּפְנֵ֥י עֲנִיִּ֖ים תִּטְחָ֑נוּ נְאֻם־ אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃ס

passages.text: The LORD also says: “Because the daughters of Zion are haughty— walking with heads held high and wanton eyes, prancing and skipping as they go, jingling the bracelets on their ankles— the Lord will bring sores on the heads of the daughters of Zion, and the LORD will make their foreheads bare.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks about the daughters of Zion.
The daughters of Zion act with pride.
They walk with their heads held high.
They look around with wanton eyes.
They walk with prancing steps.
They skip as they go.
They make their ankle bracelets jingle as they walk.
The Lord will punish the daughters of Zion.
The Lord will bring sores on their heads.
The LORD will make their foreheads bare.
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֗ה יַ֚עַן כִּ֤י גָֽבְהוּ֙ בְּנ֣וֹת צִיּ֔וֹן וַתֵּלַ֙כְנָה֙ נְטוּוֹת גָּר֔וֹן וּֽמְשַׂקְּר֖וֹת עֵינָ֑יִם הָל֤וֹךְ וְטָפֹף֙ תֵּלַ֔כְנָה וּבְרַגְלֵיהֶ֖ם תְּעַכַּֽסְנָה׃ וְשִׂפַּ֣ח אֲדֹנָ֔י קָדְקֹ֖ד בְּנ֣וֹת צִיּ֑וֹן וַיהוָ֖ה פָּתְהֵ֥ן יְעָרֶֽה׃ס

passages.text: In that day the Lord will take away their finery: their anklets and headbands and crescents; their pendants, bracelets, and veils; their headdresses, ankle chains, and sashes; their perfume bottles and charms; their signet rings and nose rings; their festive robes, capes, cloaks, and purses; and their mirrors, linen garments, tiaras, and shawls.
passages.sermon:
The Lord is the God of Hosts.
He will act on a certain day.
On that day, the Lord will take away the finery of the daughters of Zion.
He will remove their anklets.
He will remove their headbands.
He will remove their crescent ornaments.
He will take away their pendants.
He will take away their bracelets.
He will take away their veils.
He will remove their headdresses.
He will remove their ankle chains.
He will remove their sashes.
He will take away their perfume bottles.
He will take away their charms.
He will remove their signet rings.
He will remove their nose rings.
He will take away their festive robes.
He will take away their capes.
He will take away their cloaks.
He will take away their purses.
He will remove their mirrors.
He will remove their linen garments.
He will remove their tiaras.
He will remove their shawls.
passages.original: בַּיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא יָסִ֣יר אֲדֹנָ֗י אֵ֣ת תִּפְאֶ֧רֶת הָעֲכָסִ֛ים וְהַשְּׁבִיסִ֖ים וְהַשַּׂהֲרֹנִֽים׃ הַנְּטִיפ֥וֹת וְהַשֵּׁיר֖וֹת וְהָֽרְעָלֽוֹת׃ הַפְּאֵרִ֤ים וְהַצְּעָדוֹת֙ וְהַקִּשֻּׁרִ֔ים וּבָתֵּ֥י הַנֶּ֖פֶשׁ וְהַלְּחָשִֽׁים׃ הַטַּבָּע֖וֹת וְנִזְמֵ֥י הָאָֽף׃ הַמַּֽחֲלָצוֹת֙ וְהַמַּ֣עֲטָפ֔וֹת וְהַמִּטְפָּח֖וֹת וְהָחֲרִיטִֽים׃ וְהַגִּלְיֹנִים֙ וְהַסְּדִינִ֔ים וְהַצְּנִיפ֖וֹת וְהָרְדִידִֽים׃

passages.text: Instead of fragrance there will be a stench; instead of a belt, a rope; instead of styled hair, baldness; instead of fine clothing, sackcloth; instead of beauty, shame.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about the daughters of Zion.
They are proud and walk with arrogance.
God will judge them for their pride.
Instead of fragrance, there will be a stench.
Instead of a belt, there will be a rope.
Instead of styled hair, there will be baldness.
Instead of fine clothing, there will be sackcloth.
Instead of beauty, there will be shame.
passages.original: וְהָיָה֩ תַ֨חַת בֹּ֜שֶׂם מַ֣ק יִֽהְיֶ֗ה וְתַ֨חַת חֲגוֹרָ֤ה נִקְפָּה֙ וְתַ֨חַת מַעֲשֶׂ֤ה מִקְשֶׁה֙ קָרְחָ֔ה וְתַ֥חַת פְּתִיגִ֖יל מַחֲגֹ֣רֶת שָׂ֑ק כִּי־ תַ֖חַת יֹֽפִי׃

passages.text: Your men will fall by the sword, and your warriors in battle.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to the people of Jerusalem.
He warns them about coming judgment.
Your men will die by the sword.
Your strong warriors will die in battle.

passages.text: And the gates of Zion will lament and mourn; destitute, she will sit on the ground.
passages.sermon:
Zion is a city.
Zion’s gates will lament.
Zion’s gates will mourn.
Zion will become destitute.
Zion will sit on the ground.
passages.original: וְאָנ֥וּ וְאָבְל֖וּ פְּתָחֶ֑יהָ וְנִקָּ֖תָה לָאָ֥רֶץ תֵּשֵֽׁב׃
